33:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
33:1.en: O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise

33:2.ar: وَٱتَّبِعۡ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
33:2.en: And follow that which is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted

33:3.ar: وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلࣰ ا
33:3.en: And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs

33:4.ar: مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلࣲ مِّن قَلۡبَيۡنِ فِي جَوۡفِهِۦۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَزۡوَٰجَكُمُ ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي تُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنۡهُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدۡعِيَآءَكُمۡ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ قَوۡلُكُم بِأَفۡوَٰهِكُمۡۖ وَٱللَّهُ يَقُولُ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَهُوَ يَهۡدِي ٱلسَّبِيلَ
33:4.en: Allah has not made for a man two hearts in his interior. And He has not made your wives whom you declare unlawful your mothers. And he has not made your adopted sons your [true] sons. That is [merely] your saying by your mouths, but Allah says the truth, and He guides to the [right] way

33:5.ar: ٱدۡعُوهُمۡ لِأٓبَآئِهِمۡ هُوَ أَقۡسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَعۡلَمُوٓاْ ءَابَآءَهُمۡ فَإِخۡوَٰنُكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَمَوَٰلِيكُمۡۚ وَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحࣱ فِيمَآ أَخۡطَأۡتُم بِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتۡ قُلُوبُكُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمًا
33:5.en: Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers - then they are [still] your brothers in religion and those entrusted to you. And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred but [only for] what your hearts intended. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful

33:6.ar: ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَوۡلَىٰ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ مِنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡۖ وَأَزۡوَٰجُهُۥٓ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡۗ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ بَعۡضُهُمۡ أَوۡلَىٰ بِبَعۡضࣲ فِي كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ إِلَّآ أَن تَفۡعَلُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَوۡلِيَآئِكُم مَّعۡرُوفࣰ اۚ كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَسۡطُورࣰ ا
33:6.en: The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves, and his wives are [in the position of] their mothers. And those of [blood] relationship are more entitled [to inheritance] in the decree of Allah than the [other] believers and the emigrants, except that you may do to your close associates a kindness [through bequest]. That was in the Book inscribed

33:7.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مِيثَٰقَهُمۡ وَمِنكَ وَمِن نُّوحࣲ وَإِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَۖ وَأَخَذۡنَا مِنۡهُم مِّيثَٰقًا غَلِيظࣰ ا
33:7.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary; and We took from them a solemn covenant

33:8.ar: لِّيَسۡـَٔلَ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ عَن صِدۡقِهِمۡۚ وَأَعَدَّ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
33:8.en: That He may question the truthful about their truth. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment

33:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذۡ جَآءَتۡكُمۡ جُنُودࣱ فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِيحࣰ ا وَجُنُودࣰ ا لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَاۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرًا
33:9.en: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when armies came to [attack] you and We sent upon them a wind and armies [of angels] you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing

33:10.ar: إِذۡ جَآءُوكُم مِّن فَوۡقِكُمۡ وَمِنۡ أَسۡفَلَ مِنكُمۡ وَإِذۡ زَاغَتِ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلۡحَنَاجِرَ وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَا۠
33:10.en: [Remember] when they came at you from above you and from below you, and when eyes shifted [in fear], and hearts reached the throats and you assumed about Allah [various] assumptions

33:11.ar: هُنَالِكَ ٱبۡتُلِيَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَزُلۡزِلُواْ زِلۡزَالࣰ ا شَدِيدࣰ ا
33:11.en: There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking

33:12.ar: وَإِذۡ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ إِلَّا غُرُورࣰ ا
33:12.en: And [remember] when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, "Allah and His Messenger did not promise us except delusion

33:13.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَٰٓأَهۡلَ يَثۡرِبَ لَا مُقَامَ لَكُمۡ فَٱرۡجِعُواْۚ وَيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُ فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلنَّبِيَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنَا عَوۡرَةࣱ وَمَا هِيَ بِعَوۡرَةٍۖ إِن يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
33:13.en: And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no stability for you [here], so return [home]." And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are unprotected," while they were not exposed. They did not intend except to flee

33:21.ar: لَّقَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ فِي رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةࣱ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلۡيَوۡمَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَ وَذَكَرَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا
33:21.en: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day and [who] remembers Allah often

33:22.ar: وَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابَ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥۚ وَمَا زَادَهُمۡ إِلَّآ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَتَسۡلِيمࣰ ا
33:22.en: And when the believers saw the companies, they said, "This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth." And it increased them only in faith and acceptance

33:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيۡنَ أُمَتِّعۡكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحۡكُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:28.en: O Prophet, say to your wives, "If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and give you a gracious release

33:29.ar: وَإِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلۡمُحۡسِنَٰتِ مِنكُنَّ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
33:29.en: But if you should desire Allah and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter - then indeed, Allah has prepared for the doers of good among you a great reward

33:30.ar: يَٰنِسَآءَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ مَن يَأۡتِ مِنكُنَّ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ مُّبَيِّنَةࣲ يُضَٰعَفۡ لَهَا ٱلۡعَذَابُ ضِعۡفَيۡنِۚ وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرࣰ ا
33:30.en: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you should commit a clear immorality - for her the punishment would be doubled two fold, and ever is that, for Allah, easy

33:31.ar: ۞وَمَن يَقۡنُتۡ مِنكُنَّ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحࣰ ا نُّؤۡتِهَآ أَجۡرَهَا مَرَّتَيۡنِ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهَا رِزۡقࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
33:31.en: And whoever of you devoutly obeys Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness - We will give her her reward twice; and We have prepared for her a noble provision

33:32.ar: يَٰنِسَآءَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ لَسۡتُنَّ كَأَحَدࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِنِ ٱتَّقَيۡتُنَّۚ فَلَا تَخۡضَعۡنَ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ فَيَطۡمَعَ ٱلَّذِي فِي قَلۡبِهِۦ مَرَضࣱ وَقُلۡنَ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّعۡرُوفࣰ ا
33:32.en: O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech [to men], lest he in whose heart is disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech

33:33.ar: وَقَرۡنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ وَأَقِمۡنَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتِينَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِعۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ تَطۡهِيرࣰ ا
33:33.en: And abide in your houses and do not display yourselves as [was] the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity [of sin], O people of the [Prophet's] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification

33:34.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡنَ مَا يُتۡلَىٰ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ لَطِيفًا خَبِيرًا
33:34.en: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted [with all things]

33:35.ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ وَٱلۡمُسۡلِمَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتِينَ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَٱلصَّٰبِرَٰتِ وَٱلۡخَٰشِعِينَ وَٱلۡخَٰشِعَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقِينَ وَٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمِينَ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمَٰتِ وَٱلۡحَٰفِظِينَ فُرُوجَهُمۡ وَٱلۡحَٰفِظَٰتِ وَٱلذَّٰكِرِينَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَٱلذَّٰكِرَٰتِ أَعَدَّ ٱللَّهُ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣰ وَأَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
33:35.en: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the obedient men and obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who do so, and the men who remember Allah often and the women who do so - for them Allah has prepared forgiveness and a great reward

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error

33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And [remember, O Muhammad], when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished

33:38.ar: مَّا كَانَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲ فِيمَا فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥۖ سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلُۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ قَدَرࣰ ا مَّقۡدُورًا
33:38.en: There is not to be upon the Prophet any discomfort concerning that which Allah has imposed upon him. [This is] the established way of Allah with those [prophets] who have passed on before. And ever is the command of Allah a destiny decreed

hXJUgv8mng0.title: Surat Al-Ahzab Summary, Part 1
hXJUgv8mng0.one_line: Al-Ahzab opens the surahs on submission: obeying Allah when the command is uncomfortable, the circumstances are dangerous, or the matter is deeply personal.
hXJUgv8mng0.summary: He places Al-Ahzab at the head of the sixth group of surahs, running to Az-Zumar, all about obedience and full surrender to Allah. Submission sounds simple, he says, but handing over one's life, wealth and preferences entirely is hard, and Al-Ahzab tests it under the hardest conditions: military, social, economic and personal. The opening four commands (taqwa, refusing to follow disbelievers and hypocrites, following revelation whole, and relying on Allah) are the formula for an obedient life. He then walks through the uncomfortable rulings: ending the Arab practice of giving adopted children one's own name, and making the Prophet's wives mothers of the believers, which gave women standing to teach and give rulings. The covenant taken from the prophets means everyone who claims truthfulness will be questioned about it. The Battle of the Confederates shows believers whose hearts reached their throats yet held firm, while hypocrites made excuses, and in that very moment Allah names the Prophet as the model. Inside the Prophet's own home, the wives are offered a choice between worldly comfort and Allah, given special commands, and told men and women carry equal responsibility. The story of Zayd and Zaynab, the one time the Prophet felt reluctance, ends with the rule that a believer finds no hardship in what Allah ordains. He asks the audience to obey without carving out exceptions.

outline.heading: Obedience when it is hard
outline.gist: Following Allah's commands is a deeper and more delicate subject than we assume, and obeying in difficult times is what saves individuals and communities.

outline.heading: The sixth group of surahs: submission from Al-Ahzab to Az-Zumar
outline.gist: Each surah in the group looks at surrender from a different angle; Al-Ahzab takes the angle of obedience under military, social, economic and personal strain.

outline.heading: Adoption and the child's true name
outline.gist: Children are called by their own fathers' names; the Arabs had used adoption to swell their tribes, and the change was uncomfortable for them.

outline.heading: The Prophet's wives as mothers of the believers
outline.gist: The status gave the wives religious, social and political protection and an upper hand among people.

outline.heading: Four opening commands that define an obedient life
outline.gist: Taqwa, not obeying disbelievers and hypocrites, following revelation word for word without exceptions, and relying on Allah while doing so.

outline.heading: Adoption ruling and why the Arabs resisted it
outline.gist: The adopted child keeps his own lineage and is raised as a ward; the tribes had gained sons without effort, so the ruling stung.

outline.heading: Mothers of the believers gave women a voice
outline.gist: No one could harm a mother of the believers; some lived long and taught and gave rulings, which unsettled many Arabs and later rulers.

outline.heading: The covenant of the prophets and the questioning of the truthful
outline.gist: Allah took a heavy covenant of following from Muhammad, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, and will ask those who claim truthfulness about it.

outline.heading: The Confederates: believers shaken, hypocrites making excuses
outline.gist: The hypocrites called the promise a delusion and asked to go home claiming their houses were exposed, when they only wanted to flee.

outline.heading: The believers' answer and the Prophet as model
outline.gist: Seeing the armies only increased the believers in faith and submission, and Allah names the Prophet as the excellent example.

outline.heading: The heavy covenant is a covenant of obedience
outline.gist: Whoever claimed in this life to follow Allah sincerely will be questioned about that claim on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Hearts reaching the throats: doubt felt but not acted on
outline.gist: Suspicions entering the believers' hearts was human; the test was whether they acted on them or held firm.

outline.heading: The example of the Prophet chosen in the hardest moment
outline.gist: Allah chose the most frightening days Madinah ever saw to tell us to follow the Prophet's way of handling hardship.

outline.heading: Inside the Prophet's home: the wives ask for more
outline.gist: The Prophet kept giving wealth away, the wives complained of their small houses, and they were offered a graceful release or Allah and the hereafter.

outline.heading: Not like other women: doubled reward and doubled accountability
outline.gist: The wives' good deeds and mistakes weigh double, and they are told to stay in their homes and avoid the display of the first jahiliyyah.

outline.heading: Equal responsibility and no choice once Allah decides
outline.gist: Muslim men and women are listed side by side with equal reward, and a believer has no say once Allah and His Messenger decide.

outline.heading: The wives' choice and the Prophet's generosity
outline.gist: There was no anger in the offer, only a fair choice; every wife chose the Prophet and did not object again.

outline.heading: Special commands for the wives and the display of jahiliyyah
outline.gist: Allah only attributes things to jahiliyyah in four places in the Quran, and placing these commands in this surah admits that they were hard.

outline.heading: Men and women equal before Allah's command
outline.gist: The Arabs were not used to it, but men and women share the same duties toward the deen, and a believer accepts a decree however hard the circumstance.

outline.heading: Zayd and Zaynab: the Prophet's private reluctance
outline.gist: The Prophet hid in himself what Allah would reveal and feared people's talk about marrying his former adopted son's wife.

outline.heading: No hardship in what Allah ordains
outline.gist: Aisha said that if he had concealed any verse it would have been this one; the lesson is to let neither Shaytan nor the self find hardship in a command.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Real submission means accepting revelation whole, with no exceptions, even when it is socially costly or personally painful.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Fear and suspicion entering the heart is human; what matters is holding firm rather than acting on it.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: The Battle of the Trench is read as the hardest test the Muslims faced and the setting Allah chose to name the Prophet as the model.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: Hypocrites mocked the promise and invented excuses to abandon the trench.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: His generosity left his own home poor, and the Quran exposes even his private reluctance in the matter of Zaynab.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty
themes.note: Covering and avoiding display are hard commands, set beside the declaration that men and women carry equal responsibility.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Lineage must stay true in adoption, and the Prophet's wives gain the standing of mothers.

hadith.gist: Aisha said that if the Messenger had concealed anything of the Quran, he would have concealed the verse about hiding in himself what Allah would reveal.

maxims: Obeying Allah in hard times is our only rescue
Accept revelation word for word, without exceptions

stories.point: Believers felt fear yet held firm, while hypocrites fled behind excuses.

stories.who: The Prophet's wives asking for more provision
stories.point: Choosing Allah and the hereafter over comfort; all of them chose the Prophet.
Even the Prophet felt reluctance, and the verse teaches there is no hardship in following Allah's decree.

takeaways: Do not treat submission to Allah as simple; check where you carve out exceptions.
When fear or doubt enters your heart in a crisis, do not act on it.
Follow the Prophet's way of handling hardship, not only his rituals.
Once Allah and His Messenger decide a matter, do not weigh whether you like it.
Do not let the self or Shaytan make a command of Allah feel like a burden.

88:1.en: Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming [event]

88:2.en: [Some] faces, that Day, will be humbled

88:4.en: They will [enter to] burn in an intensely hot Fire

88:5.en: They will be given drink from a boiling spring

88:6.ar: لَّيۡسَ لَهُمۡ طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِن ضَرِيعࣲ‏
88:6.en: For them there will be no food except from a poisonous, thorny plant

88:7.ar: لَّا يُسۡمِنُ وَلَا يُغۡنِي مِن جُوعࣲ‏
88:7.en: Which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger

88:8.en: [Other] faces, that Day, will show pleasure

88:11.en: Wherein they will hear no unsuitable speech

88:12.en: Within it is a flowing spring

88:13.en: Within it are couches raised high

88:17.ar: أَفَلَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡإِبِلِ كَيۡفَ خُلِقَتۡ
88:17.en: Then do they not look at the camels - how they are created

88:18.en: And at the sky - how it is raised

88:19.en: And at the mountains - how they are erected

88:20.en: And at the earth - how it is spread out

88:21.en: So remind, [O Muhammad]; you are only a reminder

88:22.en: You are not over them a controller

88:23.en: However, he who turns away and disbelieves

88:24.en: Then Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment

88:25.en: Indeed, to Us is their return

88:26.en: Then indeed, upon Us is their account

Bpp18jrjiB8.speaker: adnan
Bpp18jrjiB8.speaker_note: Surah Summaries series at MWN, his cluster framing and voice throughout
Bpp18jrjiB8.title: Surah Al-Ghashiyah Summary
Bpp18jrjiB8.one_line: Revealed at the Prophet's lowest hour, Al-Ghashiyah gives the believer's third tool: relentless striving for Allah until death, since nothing here compares to the Overwhelming Event.
Bpp18jrjiB8.summary: He presents Al-Ghashiyah as the third surah in a cluster about the toolkit faith gives a believer, and its tool is mujahadah: sticking to your mission for Allah no matter how often you fail. Ordinary perseverance lasts until a person gets tired and moves on; faith-based perseverance has no off switch except losing faith, which is what baffled the Prophet's opponents. To show how the surah teaches this he sets its revelation in the year of grief: the boycott of Banu Hashim, the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah, the rejection at Taif and being barred from Makkah, the day the Prophet himself called his worst. At that moment Allah asks whether he has heard of the Overwhelming Event, where faces labour and exhaust themselves in worship that no one records any more, like writing an exam after time is called. Hardship in this life always has some light because deeds are still being recorded. The joyful faces are pleased with their sa'y, the striving they kept up until death even if the goal was never reached. The believer's job is to remind, not to control people or decide their punishment, and to keep going whether or not anyone listens.

outline.heading: The third cluster: the toolkit faith gives you
outline.gist: After surahs on fundamentals and on choices, this group lists tools Islam gives for facing life that upbringing and experience alone cannot.

outline.heading: Al-Ghashiyah's tool: mujahadah
outline.gist: After the first two tools, this surah gives continuing struggle for the sake of Allah, mujahadah or musabarah.

outline.heading: Life's perseverance versus faith's perseverance
outline.gist: Life teaches you to try for a while and then move on; faith tells you that once you know your mission you never stop, whatever happens.

outline.heading: The Prophet had no off button
outline.gist: His opponents could not understand his relentlessness through every kind of abuse; the only thing that stops a believer is losing the faith itself.

outline.heading: Revealed in the year of grief
outline.gist: The surah's depth depends on knowing it came in the tenth year of prophethood, the year of grief.

outline.heading: The boycott of Banu Hashim
outline.gist: For three years his clan was cut off from food, trade, marriage and travel, confined between two hills of Makkah.

outline.heading: Losing Abu Talib and Khadijah
outline.gist: Within a month he lost his protector outside the house and his first believer and supporter inside it.

outline.heading: Rejection at Taif and being barred from Makkah
outline.gist: Seeking support from the nearest power, he was rejected rudely and then denied re-entry to Makkah; one difficulty after another.

outline.heading: His worst day, and the question of the surah
outline.gist: He told Aisha his worst day was not Uhud but walking aimlessly back from Taif; at that hour came: has the tale of the Overwhelming Event reached you?

outline.heading: Al-Ghashiyah: the event with no way out
outline.gist: The word means what smothers and suffocates; feeling low is human, but Allah asks whether what you face now compares with that.

outline.heading: Labouring, weary faces: worship that no one records
outline.gist: On that day people finally work hard at prayer and dua with all their heart, but the book is sealed and no one is listening; that is true distress.

outline.heading: Burning fire, boiling drink, food that does not nourish
outline.gist: After all that effort they are taken to the Fire; compare and ask which is harder.

outline.heading: The joyful faces
outline.gist: All the stress and pain of striving now is for a day of soft, relaxed, joyful faces.

outline.heading: Be humbled in this world, not on that day
outline.gist: Humility before Allah, knowing we can never repay what we were given, belongs in this life; arriving at it on that day is too late.

outline.heading: Here there is always light: your deeds are still recorded
outline.gist: Even a terminal situation in this world holds hope because what you say and do is still written for you.

outline.heading: The exam after time is called
outline.gist: The best answer ever written counts for nothing once time is up; the same holds on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Pleased with their sa'y, not just their deeds
outline.gist: Sa'y is the striving toward a vision of good that one may never complete; you are rewarded for it in full whether or not you saw its fruits.

outline.heading: Memorizing the Quran an ayah a day
outline.gist: If you die still memorizing, it counts as striving toward the whole; if you stop, only what you memorized is counted.

outline.heading: Keep going until you meet Allah; the lofty garden
outline.gist: Striving only counts as sa'y if you die still doing it; its reward is a high garden where no idle word is heard.

outline.heading: Springs, raised couches, cups and carpets
outline.gist: Paradise is pictured as rest and comfort because the person worked hard until death.

outline.heading: What if the Prophet had given up?
outline.gist: After the boycott, the deaths and Taif, he could have said he could not continue; the surah tells him what is truly hard and that the happy ones are those who stuck to it.

outline.heading: Look at the camel, the sky, the mountains, the earth
outline.gist: Creation has been set up so you can live comfortably and do your job.

outline.heading: Your job is to remind
outline.gist: Speak the truth, educate and raise awareness about Allah; that is the job.

outline.heading: You are not a controller over them
outline.gist: Muslims must drop the urge to control people; a teacher offers knowledge and lets people decide, and pushing a personal agenda is corruption.

outline.heading: They are not listening. So what?
outline.gist: Being ignored was never a reason to stop; keep walking the course however heavy it gets, because the Overwhelming Event is heavier.

outline.heading: Dua and sujood into nothingness
outline.gist: On that day their dua is not received and they cannot prostrate, because they were asked to do it in this life.

outline.heading: Leave the punishment to Allah
outline.gist: Those who turn away will be punished by Allah Himself; our task is to remind, teach and be an example, and their return and reckoning are His.

outline.heading: The third tool: grit until you meet Allah
outline.gist: Only believers keep going regardless of changing circumstances; that relentlessness is the tool the surah gives.

themes.label: Mujahadah: striving as a way of life
themes.note: Faith-based perseverance has no stopping point short of losing faith.

themes.label: Mujahadah: striving as a way of life
themes.note: Sa'y is striving kept up until death, rewarded in full even when the goal is never reached.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: The year of grief, the boycott, two deaths and Taif frame the surah's message.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Effort after the record is sealed is worthless; humility and hard work belong in this life.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Any worldly hardship still has light because deeds are recorded, unlike the Overwhelming Event.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: The job is to remind, not to control people or decide their punishment, and to keep going whether or not they listen.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Feel humbled before Allah now, not on the Day of Judgment.

hadith.gist: Aisha asked the Prophet whether any day was worse than Uhud; he said the worst was the day at Taif, when he walked back not knowing where he was going

maxims: General perseverance is life; this is faith
There is no off button except losing your faith
Your job is to remind, not to control
At least now someone is recording what you do
Leave the punishment part to Allah

stories.point: Part of the backdrop of extreme hardship in which the surah came.

stories.who: Deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah
stories.point: He lost his protector and his closest supporter in one year.
His lowest hour was met with the reminder that nothing here compares to the Overwhelming Event, so keep going.

takeaways: Once you know your mission for Allah, keep at it however often you fail
Set long-term goals of good and keep striving toward them until death
Measure today's hardship against the Overwhelming Event
Remind and teach without trying to control people or judge their fate
Do your worship and humble yourself now, while it is still recorded

31:2.en: These are verses of the wise Book

31:3.en: As guidance and mercy for the doers of good

31:4.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُم بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ يُوقِنُونَ
31:4.en: Who establish prayer and give zakah, and they, of the Hereafter, are certain [in faith]

31:5.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدࣰ ى مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
31:5.en: Those are on [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful

31:6.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشۡتَرِي لَهۡوَ ٱلۡحَدِيثِ لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲ وَيَتَّخِذَهَا هُزُوًاۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
31:6.en: And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [others] from the way of Allah without knowledge and who takes it in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment

31:7.ar: وَإِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ ءَايَٰتُنَا وَلَّىٰ مُسۡتَكۡبِرࣰ ا كَأَن لَّمۡ يَسۡمَعۡهَا كَأَنَّ فِيٓ أُذُنَيۡهِ وَقۡرࣰ اۖ فَبَشِّرۡهُ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
31:7.en: And when our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as if he had not heard them, as if there was in his ears deafness. So give him tidings of a painful punishment

31:8.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُمۡ جَنَّٰتُ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
31:8.en: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them are the Gardens of Pleasure

31:9.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۖ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣰّ اۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
31:9.en: Wherein they abide eternally; [it is] the promise of Allah [which is] truth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise

31:10.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ عَمَدࣲ تَرَوۡنَهَاۖ وَأَلۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ رَوَٰسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمۡ وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَآبَّةࣲۚ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجࣲ كَرِيمٍ
31:10.en: He created the heavens without pillars that you see and has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shift with you, and dispersed therein from every creature. And We sent down rain from the sky and made grow therein [plants] of every noble kind

31:11.ar: هَٰذَا خَلۡقُ ٱللَّهِ فَأَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦۚ بَلِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
31:11.en: This is the creation of Allah. So show Me what those other than Him have created. Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error

31:12.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا لُقۡمَٰنَ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِلَّهِۚ وَمَن يَشۡكُرۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدࣱ‏
31:12.en: And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom [and said], "Be grateful to Allah." And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever denies [His favor] - then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy

31:13.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ لُقۡمَٰنُ لِٱبۡنِهِۦ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُۥ يَٰبُنَيَّ لَا تُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّ ٱلشِّرۡكَ لَظُلۡمٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
31:13.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, "O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allah. Indeed, association [with him] is great injustice

31:14.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ وَهۡنًا عَلَىٰ وَهۡنࣲ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ فِي عَامَيۡنِ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِي وَلِوَٰلِدَيۡكَ إِلَيَّ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
31:14.en: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him, [increasing her] in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the [final] destination

31:15.ar: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَاۖ وَصَاحِبۡهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَعۡرُوفࣰ اۖ وَٱتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ مَنۡ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
31:15.en: But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do

31:16.ar: يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ مِثۡقَالَ حَبَّةࣲ مِّنۡ خَرۡدَلࣲ فَتَكُن فِي صَخۡرَةٍ أَوۡ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَأۡتِ بِهَا ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
31:16.en: [And Luqman said], "O my son, indeed if wrong should be the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or [anywhere] in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted

31:17.ar: يَٰبُنَيَّ أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأۡمُرۡ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَٱنۡهَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَصَابَكَۖ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ عَزۡمِ ٱلۡأُمُورِ
31:17.en: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, [all] that is of the matters [requiring] determination

31:18.ar: وَلَا تُصَعِّرۡ خَدَّكَ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَمۡشِ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَرَحًاۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخۡتَالࣲ فَخُورࣲ‏
31:18.en: And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people and do not walk through the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful

31:19.ar: وَٱقۡصِدۡ فِي مَشۡيِكَ وَٱغۡضُضۡ مِن صَوۡتِكَۚ إِنَّ أَنكَرَ ٱلۡأَصۡوَٰتِ لَصَوۡتُ ٱلۡحَمِيرِ
31:19.en: And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys

31:20.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَسۡبَغَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعَمَهُۥ ظَٰهِرَةࣰ وَبَاطِنَةࣰۗ وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِي ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲ وَلَا هُدࣰ ى وَلَا كِتَٰبࣲ مُّنِيرࣲ‏
31:20.en: Do you not see that Allah has made subject to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and amply bestowed upon you His favors, [both] apparent and unapparent? But of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book [from Him]

31:21.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَا وَجَدۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ يَدۡعُوهُمۡ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
31:21.en: And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers." Even if Satan was inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze

31:22.ar: ۞وَمَن يُسۡلِمۡ وَجۡهَهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحۡسِنࣱ فَقَدِ ٱسۡتَمۡسَكَ بِٱلۡعُرۡوَةِ ٱلۡوُثۡقَىٰۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡأُمُورِ
31:22.en: And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good - then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to Allah will be the outcome of [all] matters

31:23.ar: وَمَن كَفَرَ فَلَا يَحۡزُنكَ كُفۡرُهُۥٓۚ إِلَيۡنَا مَرۡجِعُهُمۡ فَنُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
31:23.en: And whoever has disbelieved - let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts

31:24.ar: نُمَتِّعُهُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا ثُمَّ نَضۡطَرُّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظࣲ‏
31:24.en: We grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a massive punishment

31:25.ar: وَلَئِن سَأَلۡتَهُم مَّنۡ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ ٱللَّهُۚ قُلِ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِۚ بَلۡ أَكۡثَرُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
31:25.en: And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "[All] praise is [due] to Allah "; but most of them do not know

31:26.ar: لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ
31:26.en: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy

31:27.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقۡلَٰمࣱ وَٱلۡبَحۡرُ يَمُدُّهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ سَبۡعَةُ أَبۡحُرࣲ مَّا نَفِدَتۡ كَلِمَٰتُ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
31:27.en: And if whatever trees upon the earth were pens and the sea [was ink], replenished thereafter by seven [more] seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

31:28.ar: مَّا خَلۡقُكُمۡ وَلَا بَعۡثُكُمۡ إِلَّا كَنَفۡسࣲ وَٰحِدَةٍۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ
31:28.en: Your creation and your resurrection will not be but as that of a single soul. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing

31:29.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلࣱّ يَجۡرِيٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ى وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
31:29.en: Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term, and that Allah, with whatever you do, is Acquainted

31:30.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ
31:30.en: That is because Allah is the Truth, and that what they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Grand

31:31.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ تَجۡرِي فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِنِعۡمَتِ ٱللَّهِ لِيُرِيَكُم مِّنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارࣲ شَكُورࣲ‏
31:31.en: Do you not see that ships sail through the sea by the favor of Allah that He may show you of His signs? Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful

31:32.ar: وَإِذَا غَشِيَهُم مَّوۡجࣱ كَٱلظُّلَلِ دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡبَرِّ فَمِنۡهُم مُّقۡتَصِدࣱۚ وَمَا يَجۡحَدُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارࣲ كَفُورࣲ‏
31:32.en: And when waves come over them like canopies, they supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, there are [some] of them who are moderate [in faith]. And none rejects Our signs except everyone treacherous and ungrateful

31:33.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡاْ يَوۡمࣰ ا لَّا يَجۡزِي وَالِدٌ عَن وَلَدِهِۦ وَلَا مَوۡلُودٌ هُوَ جَازٍ عَن وَالِدِهِۦ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّۖ فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
31:33.en: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the worldly life delude you and be not deceived about Allah by the Deceiver

31:34.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُۥ عِلۡمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ ٱلۡغَيۡثَ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسࣱ مَّاذَا تَكۡسِبُ غَدࣰ اۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسُۢ بِأَيِّ أَرۡضࣲ تَمُوتُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرُۢ
31:34.en: Indeed, Allah [alone] has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul perceives in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted

ajidMJIHuAI.speaker: adnan
ajidMJIHuAI.speaker_note: his surah-summary series; refers to al-Rum covered the night before
ajidMJIHuAI.title: Surat Luqman Summary
ajidMJIHuAI.one_line: Surat Luqman as a guide to relationships between generations, built on wisdom: how parents raise children and how children treat parents.
ajidMJIHuAI.summary: He places Luqman in the cluster from al-Qasas to as-Sajdah about our relationships: with others' stories, with trials, with Allah's laws in the universe, and here between generations. Luqman is one of only two non-prophets with a surah named after them, honoured because he was an educator of generations, and education requires wisdom. The surah opens with those who buy idle talk, which he links to the recklessness of youth and also to preachers who lack wisdom, raising unimportant religious topics that make young people lose interest or mock the deen. Duty to parents continues even if they push you away from Islam: you do not obey them in that, but you remain the best companion to them. From Luqman's advice he draws a method for parents: speak tenderly; introduce your child to Allah first; ask for one core ritual, prayer, rather than overloading them; encourage social participation in good; teach patience at home before the world tests them; teach humility and manners with vivid images and humour, as with the donkey's voice. He warns that following forefathers is not always right: parents may not use birr to dictate a child's university or residence, and children must not follow harmful traditions. Wisdom, knowledge joined to experience, is endless like Allah's words.

outline.heading: A cluster of surahs about relationships
outline.gist: Relationships are among the most important aspects of human life.

outline.heading: Relationships with stories, trials, cosmic laws and generations
outline.gist: The earlier surahs treat our relationship with others' stories, with calamities and with Allah's laws; Luqman turns to generations.

outline.heading: Recap of al-Qasas, al-Ankabut and ar-Rum
outline.gist: Each surah of the group addresses one relationship in our surroundings.

outline.heading: Why a surah is named after Luqman
outline.gist: Apart from Maryam he is the only non-prophet so honoured, because he was an educator of generations.

outline.heading: Education requires wisdom: the book of wisdom
outline.gist: The surah opens by pointing to wisdom.

outline.heading: Idle talk and the recklessness of youth
outline.gist: Lack of wisdom leads to wasted talk and mockery of serious matters, including careless talk about religion.

outline.heading: Idle talk that leads away from Allah's path
outline.gist: Young people by nature waste time in talk that brings no benefit and distances them from Allah.

outline.heading: Unwise preaching turns youth away
outline.gist: Choosing unimportant religious topics, or the wrong time and way, makes the next generation lose interest and mock even valid teachings.

outline.heading: Luqman's wisdom, gratitude and duty to parents
outline.gist: The mother's burden, and remaining their best companion even if they push you away from Islam.

outline.heading: Good companionship with parents even when you cannot obey
outline.gist: Knowing our duties to those above and below us holds society together.

outline.heading: Advice given tenderly: do not associate partners
outline.gist: Wa'z means advising with kindness and gentleness.

outline.heading: The mustard seed: Allah is subtle and aware
outline.gist: Nothing escapes Allah, wherever it is hidden.

outline.heading: Prayer, enjoining good, and patience
outline.gist: Commanding good and forbidding wrong as participation in social reform; life brings misfortunes that require perseverance.

outline.heading: Do not turn your cheek or strut; be moderate
outline.gist: Visual images help young people grasp the lesson.

outline.heading: The donkey's voice: humour to reach a child
outline.gist: Luqman likely used humour to relate to his son; advice begins with tenderness.

outline.heading: Introduce children to Allah first; one ritual is enough
outline.gist: Ask for prayer at this age rather than overloading children with rituals.

outline.heading: Social participation and patience learned at home
outline.gist: Push children to take part in good, and teach patience before the first calamity outside the home overwhelms them.

outline.heading: Humility and manners taught with vivid images
outline.gist: Walk calmly and speak softly; young people respond to imagery and humour.

outline.heading: Following forefathers: when parents press harmful traditions
outline.gist: Young people pressured to keep cultural practices they see as wrong.

outline.heading: Trees as pens: wisdom never runs out
outline.gist: There is always more wisdom and experience to gain in dealing with parents and children.

outline.heading: Limits of what parents may demand
outline.gist: Do not follow harmful traditions just because parents command them, and parents may not invoke birr to choose a child's university or home.

outline.heading: A day when no father avails his son
outline.gist: Generations had their chance in this world to benefit one another.

outline.heading: The keys of the unseen
outline.gist: Knowledge of the Hour, rain, the womb, tomorrow and the place of death belong to Allah.

outline.heading: Wisdom is knowledge joined to experience
outline.gist: Either alone falls short; Allah, the Wise, teaches us how generations should deal with one another.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.note: Luqman's method: tenderness, Allah first, one ritual, social participation, patience, manners taught with imagery and humour.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Stay a good companion to parents even when you cannot obey them.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Parents cannot use birr to impose harmful traditions or life choices outside their right.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: The recklessness of youth and how unwise religious talk pushes them away.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Choose topics, timing and manner that matter to the audience.

themes.label: Commanding good and forbidding wrong (amr bil-ma'ruf)
themes.note: Understood as participation in social reform.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Wisdom combines knowledge with experience.

maxims: Wisdom is knowledge plus experience
Introduce your children to Allah first
Prayer is enough as the first ritual
Parents may not use birr for what Allah did not command

stories.point: A model of raising children with tenderness, priorities and humour.

contemporary: Children of immigrant parents pressured to keep cultural traditions
Parents choosing their children's university studies or place of residence
takeaways: Advise your children gently and start by teaching them who Allah is.
Do not overload young people with rituals; prioritize prayer.
Teach children patience and social responsibility at home before the world tests them.
Remain kind and present with your parents even when you cannot follow them.
When teaching religion to youth, pick what matters to them now.

61:1.ar: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
61:1.en: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allah, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise

61:2.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
61:2.en: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do

61:3.ar: كَبُرَ مَقۡتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا لَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
61:3.en: Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do

61:4.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِۦ صَفࣰّ ا كَأَنَّهُم بُنۡيَٰنࣱ مَّرۡصُوصࣱ‏
61:4.en: Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row as though they are a [single] structure joined firmly

61:5.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوۡمِهِۦ يَٰقَوۡمِ لِمَ تُؤۡذُونَنِي وَقَد تَّعۡلَمُونَ أَنِّي رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيۡكُمۡۖ فَلَمَّا زَاغُوٓاْ أَزَاغَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
61:5.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Moses said to his people, "O my people, why do you harm me while you certainly know that I am the messenger of Allah to you?" And when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people

61:6.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيۡكُم مُّصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَمُبَشِّرَۢا بِرَسُولࣲ يَأۡتِي مِنۢ بَعۡدِي ٱسۡمُهُۥٓ أَحۡمَدُۖ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا سِحۡرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
61:6.en: And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, "O children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad." But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, "This is obvious magic

61:10.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ تِجَٰرَةࣲ تُنجِيكُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
61:10.en: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment

61:11.ar: تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُمۡ وَأَنفُسِكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
61:11.en: [It is that] you believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you should know

61:12.ar: يَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡ ذُنُوبَكُمۡ وَيُدۡخِلۡكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ وَمَسَٰكِنَ طَيِّبَةࣰ فِي جَنَّٰتِ عَدۡنࣲۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
61:12.en: He will forgive for you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great attainment

61:13.ar: وَأُخۡرَىٰ تُحِبُّونَهَاۖ نَصۡرࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَتۡحࣱ قَرِيبࣱۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
61:13.en: And [you will obtain] another [favor] that you love - victory from Allah and an imminent conquest; and give good tidings to the believers

61:14.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُوٓاْ أَنصَارَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ لِلۡحَوَارِيِّـۧنَ مَنۡ أَنصَارِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ ٱلۡحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحۡنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِۖ فَـَٔامَنَت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنۢ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَكَفَرَت طَّآئِفَةࣱۖ فَأَيَّدۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ عَلَىٰ عَدُوِّهِمۡ فَأَصۡبَحُواْ ظَٰهِرِينَ
61:14.en: O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah, as when Jesus, the son of Mary, said to the disciples, "Who are my supporters for Allah?" The disciples said, "We are supporters of Allah." And a faction of the Children of Israel believed and a faction disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant

62:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
62:2.en: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom - although they were before in clear error

62:5.ar: مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ حُمِّلُواْ ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةَ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَحۡمِلُوهَا كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡحِمَارِ يَحۡمِلُ أَسۡفَارَۢاۚ بِئۡسَ مَثَلُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
62:5.en: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not take it on is like that of a donkey who carries volumes [of books]. Wretched is the example of the people who deny the signs of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people

62:6.ar: قُلۡ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوٓاْ إِن زَعَمۡتُمۡ أَنَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءُ لِلَّهِ مِن دُونِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُاْ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
62:6.en: Say, "O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of Allah, excluding the [other] people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful

62:7.ar: وَلَا يَتَمَنَّوۡنَهُۥٓ أَبَدَۢا بِمَا قَدَّمَتۡ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
62:7.en: But they will not wish for it, ever, because of what their hands have put forth. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers

62:8.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ ٱلَّذِي تَفِرُّونَ مِنۡهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ مُلَٰقِيكُمۡۖ ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَٰلِمِ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
62:8.en: Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do

62:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَوٰةِ مِن يَوۡمِ ٱلۡجُمُعَةِ فَٱسۡعَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَذَرُواْ ٱلۡبَيۡعَۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
62:9.en: O you who have believed, when [the adhan] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumu'ah [Friday], then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew

62:10.ar: فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةُ فَٱنتَشِرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
62:10.en: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may succeed

62:11.ar: وَإِذَا رَأَوۡاْ تِجَٰرَةً أَوۡ لَهۡوًا ٱنفَضُّوٓاْ إِلَيۡهَا وَتَرَكُوكَ قَآئِمࣰ اۚ قُلۡ مَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهۡوِ وَمِنَ ٱلتِّجَٰرَةِۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
62:11.en: But when they saw a transaction or a diversion, [O Muhammad], they rushed to it and left you standing. Say, "What is with Allah is better than diversion and than a transaction, and Allah is the best of providers

AowhDlUVZuc.speaker: adnan
AowhDlUVZuc.speaker_note: His own surah-summary lesson: compares the 10-20 people at his lessons with the full masjid at the khutbah he gives, and calls khutbah misuse 'a pet peeve of mine'.
AowhDlUVZuc.title: Surat As-Saff and Al-Jumu'ah: Summaries
AowhDlUVZuc.one_line: As-Saff as a contract to put the ummah before yourself; Al-Jumu'ah as Islam's built-in system of leadership that Muslims are wasting.
AowhDlUVZuc.summary: A Sunday lesson summarizing two Medinan surahs of the 28th juz, which he describes as organizing Muslim society. As-Saff, he says, is built around a contract. It opens by rebuking believers who say what they do not do: having joined the ummah, you committed to put its interest before your own. Fighters standing in a row like a solid structure is the Quran's ultimate example of that sacrifice, and the prayer row symbolizes the same unity. Musa's and Isa's peoples failed because self-interest divided them, which is also why they rejected the prophet Isa foretold as Ahmad. The surah's centre is the 'trade' of 61:10-13: give your wealth and yourself, receive forgiveness, Paradise and victory. Its close calls believers to be helpers of Allah as the disciples and the Ansar were. Al-Jumu'ah, he argues, installs a system of leadership in Islam: the khateeb inherits the four tasks of the prophets in 62:2, so khutbahs must be relevant, simple and purposeful. A billion people gathering weekly with so little progress shows how badly the platform is wasted, and Muslims who own a heritage they never read are the donkey carrying books.

outline.heading: The Medinan cluster of the 28th juz
outline.gist: These surahs, all revealed in Madinah, organize Muslim life: relations among Muslims, with non-Muslims near and far, with enemies and traitors, with fellow citizens and spouses, along with leadership and domestic law.

outline.heading: A surah built on a contract
outline.gist: As-Saff revolves around a verse offering a contract: keep the commitment you made on becoming Muslim to hold the group together and serve its message. Organizing a large people calls for a contract.

outline.heading: Why do you say what you do not do?
outline.gist: After the opening glorification comes the axis of the surah: saying what you do not do is hateful to Allah. At the level of society, you joined the ummah and pledged to work for its unity, service and success in every field, so why are you not doing it?

outline.heading: The solid row
outline.gist: Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row like a solid structure. Combat is rarely what is asked, but it is the Quran's ultimate example of putting the ummah's interest before your own; the prayer row is a symbol of the same oneness and care for one another.

outline.heading: Musa's people: self-interest over the nation
outline.gist: Musa asks why his people harm him. He sets aside specific tafsir narrations that lack authenticity for the charge the Quran repeats about 25 times: they divided, became egocentric rather than nation-centred, and when they deviated Allah turned their hearts away.

outline.heading: Isa foretells Ahmad
outline.gist: Isa confirms the Torah and foretells a messenger after him named Ahmad, the only place the Prophet is so named. His people refused him because following him meant giving up something of themselves for the bigger picture.

outline.heading: The trade that saves from a painful punishment
outline.gist: Allah's business proposal: believe, and exhaust your wealth, time and lives in His cause; in return, forgiveness, the highest ranks of Paradise and the thing you love, victory and prosperity. Putting the ummah before your likes, dislikes and happiness is the contract in the Quran: have you signed it?

outline.heading: Be helpers of Allah
outline.gist: Do not just say you believe and pray: be ansar of Allah, those who stand by and strengthen His message, as the people of Madinah were named for standing by the Prophet and as the disciples answered Isa. Those who signed the contract and lived by it prevailed.

outline.heading: Interlude
Leadership comes installed with Islam
outline.gist: Al-Jumu'ah is about leadership: Islam comes with a built-in system you only need to activate. Any few Muslims anywhere, from Alaska to the Amazon, find each other, build a masjid and hold Jumuah, and whoever gives it is the one who leads and decides.

outline.heading: A billion people a week and no progress
outline.gist: Around a billion people gather every week, even virtually during Covid; no other group does this. If those messages had benefit, structure and unity, how could Muslims fail to progress? Muslims must be professionals at ruining things.

outline.heading: The khateeb takes the prophets' role
outline.gist: 62:2 lists the four reasons prophets were sent, and the khateeb inherits them. He should not be handed a paper to read or speak on issues irrelevant to the people in front of him; Jumuah was how the Prophet and the companions led communities, and everything the ummah needs can happen there.

outline.heading: Allah gathers them; offer a message worth hearing
outline.gist: His lessons draw ten to twenty people while his khutbah fills the masjid, not for him but because Allah obliges them to come, so the khateeb is obliged to deliver and will be held to account. Tell people about Allah, help them purify themselves, teach the rulings and the wisdom to practise them, without controversial detail.

outline.heading: The donkey carrying books
outline.gist: Those given the Torah who did not live by it are like a donkey loaded with books. Descending from a heritage that united science and religion, with over 300,000 Islamic books and the Quran for 1,400 years, means nothing if you read and reflect on none of it.

outline.heading: When the Jumuah narrative dies
outline.gist: When Jumuah stops doing its job, people are Muslim only by birth and feel no connection; youth find it more meaningless each week and come only because they must, which cannot last. The leadership system is there for the taking.

outline.heading: Wish for death, then
outline.gist: Being given guidance, being born Muslim or speaking Arabic does not make you Allah's ally. Claim it and wish for death; no one does, because all know how far they are. Death will find you, so use your time well.

outline.heading: Allah does His part: the Friday call
outline.gist: With one verse Allah gathers a billion people every week, by a generous estimate; with that much in common, failing to progress is baffling.

outline.heading: Leave trade, then seek His bounty
outline.gist: At the call, leave buying and selling; after the prayer, go out and work, seeking Allah's bounty and remembering Him throughout, carrying the message you heard.

outline.heading: The caravan that left him standing
outline.gist: Early on, when a trade caravan arrived during the khutbah, people left the Prophet standing; it took time to teach that Jumuah outranks livelihood and distraction, since Allah provides. Keep your priorities straight and listen to your leader.

outline.heading: Jumuah left a skeleton
outline.gist: Leadership and proper narratives have been taken out of Jumuah, leaving a skeleton of what it was; it can return. Allah gathers people not for His sake but for their benefit: this is how a society is built and strengthened.

outline.heading: Outro

apeX4BUhbFU.speaker: adnan
apeX4BUhbFU.speaker_note: his Surah Summaries series on the short surahs at MWN; single teacher throughout
apeX4BUhbFU.title: Surah Summaries: Al-Zalzalah and Al-Adiyat
apeX4BUhbFU.one_line: Al-Zalzalah: Earth testifies against her children and judgment rests on simple good and evil; Al-Adiyat: the horse's loyalty shames human disloyalty to Allah.
apeX4BUhbFU.summary: He frames the final surahs as small concentrated doses of Islamic values. Al-Zalzalah, he says, is a single snapshot of the Day of Judgment: the earth, the one constant every human leans on and the mother of all people equally, convulses, expels the dead and then tells her stories. She reports what her children did to one another and also what they did to her, the polluted rivers, the felled trees, the ruined air. Hearing a harsh truth from someone so close is what leaves people walking dazed. Judgment then rests on an atom's weight of good and evil, measured by an innate moral sense that every human has before religion confirms it. Were you a force of goodness, of evil, or a mixture? Al-Adiyat carries one idea, loyalty. Its oaths paint a short film of panting horses striking sparks and charging into an army at dawn with no hesitation, though their owner gave them only food and water. The human, given far more by Allah, is kanud, a word joining disloyalty and ingratitude. We stay loyal only while life goes our way, and like Ibn Rawahah at Mu'tah even a moment's hesitation costs rank. He asks the audience to stop asking for more and start giving back their time, empathy, expertise and wealth.

outline.heading: The short surahs as concentrated pills of Islamic values
outline.gist: Each final surah condenses what longer surahs explain at length, so knowing them gives a person the core values needed to reach Allah.

outline.heading: Both surahs early Makkan; Al-Zalzalah is about judgment
outline.gist: Both were revealed early in Makkah. Al-Zalzalah teaches accountability and specifically what judgment will be based on.

outline.heading: The Quran shows the Last Day in snapshots
outline.gist: No single passage narrates the whole Day of Judgment; each surah gives a snapshot, and this one is the earth's testimony on which judgment rests.

outline.heading: The earth convulses and throws out her burdens
outline.gist: The great quake expels everyone from their graves. Earth is the one constant we lean on, and every human, of every race, is equally her child.

outline.heading: What is wrong with her? When the constant breaks
outline.gist: Earth has always sheltered and fed us; when she breaks the norm, nothing is certain anymore, and that is what shocks the human being.

outline.heading: She tells her stories: how her children treated each other
outline.gist: Earth witnessed every deed done in private, and she will report the killing, oppression and cruelty, all of which grieve a mother whoever is fighting.

outline.heading: She also tells what we did to her
outline.gist: She will complain of polluted rivers, cut trees and ruined air: her children were unkind to one another and to their own mother.

outline.heading: People emerge scattered, hurt by the harsh truth
outline.gist: A harsh truth from someone very close wounds deeply and is never forgotten; hearing every truth about our greed and extravagance leaves people walking aimlessly.

outline.heading: An atom's weight: judgment by simple good and evil
outline.gist: Earth does not care about sectarian and theological divisions. Humans know good and evil innately; religion confirms it and gives it intention.

outline.heading: Earth's final testimony before she passes
outline.gist: Having served humanity for billions of years, earth gives her last testimony; who judges children better than their mother? Were you a force of good, evil or both?

outline.heading: Al-Adiyat: a linguistic masterpiece on loyalty
outline.gist: The surah carries one thought only, loyalty, and expresses it in breathtaking language.

outline.heading: The oaths as a short film: panting chargers striking sparks
outline.gist: The oaths draw a picture of horses galloping so hard their breathing is audible and their hooves strike sparks from rock; he takes a question on whether horses or camels are meant and says it makes little difference.

outline.heading: The dawn raid: dust raised and straight into the army
outline.gist: They attack at dawn, raise a storm of dust and charge fearlessly into the middle of an enemy host.

outline.heading: What did you ever give the horse?
outline.gist: Its owner gave it only food, water and a pat, yet it never hesitates or questions being ridden toward death. Its loyalty is complete.

outline.heading: Kanud: disloyal and ungrateful in one word
outline.gist: The human being is kanud toward his Lord, the one word in Arabic that joins disloyalty with ingratitude. Allah has given us far more than we ever gave an animal.

outline.heading: Loyal only while things go our way
outline.gist: One curve ball and we question everything despite years of blessings. A rider cannot work with a horse that hesitates; Allah says trust me and keep going.

outline.heading: Mu'tah: the cost of a second's hesitation
outline.gist: Zayd and Ja'far held the banner until death; Abdullah ibn Rawahah hesitated for a moment before fighting, and the Prophet described his rank as slightly below theirs.

outline.heading: We always want a little more
outline.gist: Picture a horse asking for one more day of food before it rides out; that is how humans bargain with Allah.

outline.heading: The 93-year-old who wanted two more years
outline.gist: A terminally ill elderly patient kept hoping for two more years and then two more. Wanting more is human, but it must not block loyalty to Allah.

outline.heading: What Allah asks back: time, empathy, expertise, wealth
outline.gist: Most will not be asked for their lives, but Allah asks for time, attention, empathy, knowledge and wealth; will we give or keep asking for more?

outline.heading: The graves overturned and the hidden exposed
outline.gist: Everything hidden in graves and in hearts is brought out; every hesitation, doubt and disloyalty will be clear to the Lord who knows all.

67:2.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلࣰ اۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
67:2.en: [He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed - and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving

67:3.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ اۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتࣲۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورࣲ‏
67:3.en: [And] who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks

67:4.ar: ثُمَّ ٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيۡنِ يَنقَلِبۡ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَصَرُ خَاسِئࣰ ا وَهُوَ حَسِيرࣱ‏
67:4.en: Then return [your] vision twice again. [Your] vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued

67:5.ar: وَلَقَدۡ زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهَا رُجُومࣰ ا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِۖ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:5.en: And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with stars and have made [from] them what is thrown at the devils and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze

67:6.ar: وَلِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ عَذَابُ جَهَنَّمَۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
67:6.en: And for those who disbelieved in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination

67:7.ar: إِذَآ أُلۡقُواْ فِيهَا سَمِعُواْ لَهَا شَهِيقࣰ ا وَهِيَ تَفُورُ
67:7.en: When they are thrown into it, they hear from it a [dreadful] inhaling while it boils up

67:8.ar: تَكَادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيۡظِۖ كُلَّمَآ أُلۡقِيَ فِيهَا فَوۡجࣱ سَأَلَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَآ أَلَمۡ يَأۡتِكُمۡ نَذِيرࣱ‏
67:8.en: It almost bursts with rage. Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did there not come to you a warner

67:9.ar: قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ قَدۡ جَآءَنَا نَذِيرࣱ فَكَذَّبۡنَا وَقُلۡنَا مَا نَزَّلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ كَبِيرࣲ‏
67:9.en: They will say," Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error

67:10.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡ كُنَّا نَسۡمَعُ أَوۡ نَعۡقِلُ مَا كُنَّا فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:10.en: And they will say, "If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze

67:11.ar: فَٱعۡتَرَفُواْ بِذَنۢبِهِمۡ فَسُحۡقࣰ ا لِّأَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:11.en: And they will admit their sin, so [it is] alienation for the companions of the Blaze

67:12.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
67:12.en: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and great reward

67:13.ar: وَأَسِرُّواْ قَوۡلَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱجۡهَرُواْ بِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
67:13.en: And conceal your speech or publicize it; indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts

67:14.ar: أَلَا يَعۡلَمُ مَنۡ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
67:14.en: Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Acquainted

67:15.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ذَلُولࣰ ا فَٱمۡشُواْ فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا وَكُلُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِهِۦۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلنُّشُورُ
67:15.en: It is He who made the earth tame for you - so walk among its slopes and eat of His provision - and to Him is the resurrection

67:16.ar: ءَأَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يَخۡسِفَ بِكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَمُورُ
67:16.en: Do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven would not cause the earth to swallow you and suddenly it would sway

67:17.ar: أَمۡ أَمِنتُم مَّن فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَن يُرۡسِلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَاصِبࣰ اۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ كَيۡفَ نَذِيرِ
67:17.en: Or do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven would not send against you a storm of stones? Then you would know how [severe] was My warning

67:18.ar: وَلَقَدۡ كَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ فَكَيۡفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ
67:18.en: And already had those before them denied, and how [terrible] was My reproach

67:19.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَوۡقَهُمۡ صَٰٓفَّٰتࣲ وَيَقۡبِضۡنَۚ مَا يُمۡسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُۚ إِنَّهُۥ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءِۭ بَصِيرٌ
67:19.en: Do they not see the birds above them with wings outspread and [sometimes] folded in? None holds them [aloft] except the Most Merciful. Indeed He is, of all things, Seeing

67:20.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ جُندࣱ لَّكُمۡ يَنصُرُكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِۚ إِنِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غُرُورٍ
67:20.en: Or who is it that could be an army for you to aid you other than the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are not but in delusion

67:21.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي يَرۡزُقُكُمۡ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَ رِزۡقَهُۥۚ بَل لَّجُّواْ فِي عُتُوࣲّ وَنُفُورٍ
67:21.en: Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision? But they have persisted in insolence and aversion

67:22.ar: أَفَمَن يَمۡشِي مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦٓ أَهۡدَىٰٓ أَمَّن يَمۡشِي سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
67:22.en: Then is one who walks fallen on his face better guided or one who walks erect on a straight path

67:23.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنشَأَكُمۡ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَ وَٱلۡأَفۡـِٔدَةَۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَشۡكُرُونَ
67:23.en: Say, "It is He who has produced you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful

67:24.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلَّذِي ذَرَأَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
67:24.en: Say, "It is He who has multiplied you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered

67:25.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلۡوَعۡدُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
67:25.en: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful

67:26.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَا ٱلۡعِلۡمُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَإِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
67:26.en: Say, "The knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner

67:27.ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوۡهُ زُلۡفَةࣰ سِيٓـَٔتۡ وُجُوهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَقِيلَ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَدَّعُونَ
67:27.en: But when they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieve will be distressed, and it will be said, "This is that for which you used to call

67:28.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَهۡلَكَنِيَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَن مَّعِيَ أَوۡ رَحِمَنَا فَمَن يُجِيرُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ مِنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
67:28.en: Say, [O Muhammad], "Have you considered: whether Allah should cause my death and those with me or have mercy upon us, who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment

67:29.ar: قُلۡ هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ وَعَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡنَاۖ فَسَتَعۡلَمُونَ مَنۡ هُوَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
67:29.en: Say, "He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. And you will [come to] know who it is that is in clear error

67:30.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِنۡ أَصۡبَحَ مَآؤُكُمۡ غَوۡرࣰ ا فَمَن يَأۡتِيكُم بِمَآءࣲ مَّعِينِۭ
67:30.en: Say, "Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water
